newsitem.title: UK: Photographer Donovan commits suicide - family.
newsitem.headline: Photographer Donovan commits suicide - family.

text.p: British fashion and society photographer Terence Donovan has committed suicide after reacting severely to medication, his family said on Saturday.
Donovan, famed for his fashion shots, pop videos and pictures of the royal family, was found hanging in his London studio.
A spokesman for Princess Diana, who had been photographed by Donovan, said she was "devastated, like all those who loved him".

Sixties fashion designer Mary Quant, a close friend, said the 60-year-old Donovan was "one of the world's greatest-ever photographers, a huge character, a man of vast affection, generosity and courage, with immense appetite for life".
His wife Diana said in a statement that Donovan was found dead at his studio in London on Friday.
"I am very sad to announce that my husband Terence tragically took his own life as a result of a severe reaction to medication.
"My husband was a quite wonderful man. My children and I are devastated," she said.
Family friend and media consultant Sir Tim Bell called Donovan one of Britain's great photographers.
"He made many television commercials and feature films as well. He photographed all of the world's top fashion models and his work appeared in every major newspaper and magazine," Bell said.
His last project was a set of photos for GQ magazine of the leading lights in British pop music.
